title: Newborn life support
stem: A woman at 38 weeks has just given birth in the ED. The baby is handed to you: floppy, not breathing, pale. You have a resuscitaire, a nurse and a junior doctor. The paediatric team is on the way.

phases.title: Prepare
phases.goal: Warmth, a clock, the bag in air, airways, a pre-ductal probe.

phases.title: Resuscitate
phases.goal: Dry and assess, open the airway, inflation breaths, fix the airway if the chest does not move, ventilate.

phases.title: After
phases.goal: SpO2 targets, warmth and glucose, handover.

phases.title: Brief and tell
phases.goal: What if the heart rate had stayed low? Then her mother.

review.text: Ventilation rate. AHA/NRP (Hong Kong neonatal courses) and your notes: 40–60 breaths a minute; RCUK: 5 inflation breaths, then 30 a minute. The bench teaches the inflation breaths and accepts 30–60 a minute.
Adrenaline. AHA: 0.01–0.03 mg/kg IV every 3–5 minutes; RCUK 2025: 20 microgram/kg every 4 minutes. The script says 20 micrograms per kg (0.02 mg/kg) every 3 to 5 minutes, inside both.
Sodium bicarbonate is no longer recommended in newborn resuscitation, and skin colour carries less weight in the first assessment.

notes:
Checked against Resuscitation Council UK Newborn Life Support 2025 (ERC 2025 NLS) and ILCOR 2025.

Sequence: start a clock; dry and wrap (plastic bag without drying if under 32 weeks), keep warm; assess tone, breathing and heart rate (2025 puts less weight on skin colour); open the airway in a neutral position. If not breathing: 5 inflation breaths (2–3 seconds each; 30 cmH2O term, 25 cmH2O preterm) in air for 32 weeks and over; reassess heart rate. If no chest movement: airway manoeuvres (two-person jaw thrust, suction under direct vision, supraglottic airway or intubation — 2025 encourages earlier supraglottic airway and videolaryngoscopy), repeat inflation breaths. Once the chest moves, ventilation breaths 30/min for 30 seconds. If the heart rate stays under 60 after 30 seconds of effective ventilation: chest compressions 3:1 (90 compressions and 30 breaths per minute) with 100% oxygen; reassess every 30 seconds. Drugs via umbilical venous catheter or IO: adrenaline 20 microgram/kg IV, repeated every 4 minutes (2025 standardised interval); consider 10 mL/kg volume and glucose. Sodium bicarbonate is no longer recommended (2025). Naloxone is not recommended.

Your notes follow the AHA 2020 neonatal algorithm (MR SOPA, PPV 40–60/min, SpO2 targets, adrenaline 0.01 mg/kg IV) and the UK 5 inflation breaths; both are close to RCUK. Differences: RCUK adrenaline 20 microgram/kg IV every 4 minutes; APGAR colour de-emphasised; bicarbonate removed.

Perfect script checked against an AHA/NRP checklist, the RCUK NLS algorithm, an HKCEM-style scheme and a keyword scheme. Removed the wrong options (100% oxygen first, bicarbonate) and the bench's two wrong-move buttons (hanging the baby, early compressions). Added: early help, MR SOPA named, SpO2 targets, warmth and glucose after, a handover, and an update to the mother. The bench accepts 30–60 ventilation breaths a minute (RCUK and AHA).

script.say: Start the clock. Heater on, warm towels and a hat. Bag set to 30 over 5 cmH2O with a term mask, in air. Suction, a size 1 supraglottic airway and a laryngoscope. Saturation probe on the right wrist: pre-ductal.
Dry her, take away the wet towel, wrap her and put the hat on; stimulate her.
script.do: Rub dry, wrap, hat, flick the soles.

script.say: Tone: floppy. Breathing: none. Heart rate with the stethoscope: about 55.
Head in the neutral position, chin supported. Five inflation breaths, 2 to 3 seconds each, at 30 cmH2O. Watching for chest rise.
No chest rise: MR SOPA. Mask and reposition; a two-person jaw thrust; suction if needed, open the mouth, more pressure, then an alternative airway. Five more inflation breaths.
script.do: Two-person jaw thrust: the chest rises.

script.say: The chest is moving: ventilation breaths for 30 seconds, then reassess the heart rate.
script.do: Heart rate 120 and rising; gasping, then crying.

script.say: Heart rate over 100 and breathing: support her breathing as needed and keep the pre-ductal SpO2 on target: 60% at 1 minute rising to 85 to 95% by 10 minutes. Keep her warm, 36.5 to 37.5 degrees, and check her glucose.

Handover to the paediatric team: term baby, born apnoeic and floppy with a heart rate of 55; five inflation breaths with a jaw thrust, then ventilation; heart rate now over 100 and breathing. For the neonatal unit.

If the heart rate stays under 60 after 30 seconds of ventilation that moves the chest: secure the airway, then compressions 3:1, 90 compressions and 30 breaths a minute, in 100% oxygen; reassess every 30 seconds.
Then an umbilical venous catheter: adrenaline 20 micrograms per kg, that's 0.02 mg/kg, every 3 to 5 minutes; and 10 mL/kg of saline if there's been blood loss.
